lines.trans: Drinking is all about willpower—my willpower is strong, so basically I hardly ever get drunk.
Even supposing I do get slightly tipsy, my drinking habits are remarkably neat.
Stop drinking now—keep going like that and you will slip up!
I can hold my liquor—stop worrying about me and pace yourself!
Whenever Ye-jin insists she is not drunk, that means she is drunk.
Did you spread rumors that I live at Joon-mo's place, or not?
You are about to spread the rumor yourself right now!
Joon-mo, let's go home!
Yes, let's each head to our own separate homes, senior!
Once she gets drunk, she has zero secrets left and turns overly cute.
Somehow she has no middle ground whatsoever—just extreme cuteness!

examples.trans: Did you hear about this drinks or something?
I was busy today because of drinks or something.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 술은 정신력이거든요, 제가 정신력이 강해서 기본적으로 잘 취하지를 않고요.
examples.trans: Drinking is all about willpower—my willpower is strong, so basically I hardly ever get drunk.
Here the word for 'is mental strength, you see' is key.

meanings.note: Humble first-person singular pronoun used in polite speech.

examples.trans: I have an induction ceremony.
Follow me.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 술은 정신력이거든요, 제가 정신력이 강해서 기본적으로 잘 취하지를 않고요.
examples.trans: Drinking is all about willpower—my willpower is strong, so basically I hardly ever get drunk.
This expression comes from 'because it is strong'.
Did you hear about this basic?
I was busy today because of basic.
Listen closely to what I explain.
I eat Korean food well.
Let's got drunk and together today.
I worked hard to got drunk and yesterday too.

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 설령 조금 취했다 해도 술버릇이 굉장히 깔끔한 편이라.
examples.trans: Even supposing I do get slightly tipsy, my drinking habits are remarkably neat.
Here the word for 'even supposing' is key.

examples.text: 티 안 내려고 무지 애는 쓰시는데 저는 조금 알 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: She tries hard not to show it, yet I think I understand that feeling a little.

examples.text: 조금만 더 가면 금방 도착할 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: If we go just a little farther, we should arrive soon.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 설령 조금 취했다 해도 술버릇이 굉장히 깔끔한 편이라.
examples.trans: Even supposing I do get slightly tipsy, my drinking habits are remarkably neat.
Here the word for 'drinking habit' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 설령 조금 취했다 해도 술버릇이 굉장히 깔끔한 편이라.
examples.trans: Even supposing I do get slightly tipsy, my drinking habits are remarkably neat.
Here the word for 'extremely, very' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adj).

examples.text: 설령 조금 취했다 해도 술버릇이 굉장히 깔끔한 편이라.
examples.trans: Even supposing I do get slightly tipsy, my drinking habits are remarkably neat.
This expression comes from 'clean, neat'.

examples.text: 그러니까 저한테 잘하셔야 돼요. 철저히 제 편, 아시겠죠?
examples.trans: So you have to treat me well. Strictly on my side, got it?
The topic of side / tendency came up during this shoot.
Do you have time today?
Where are you going?

meanings.note: Used only with close friends, younger people, or children
used before a verb to tell someone to stop an ongoing action

examples.trans: Stop worrying now.
I'm so full I'll stop eating.
I want to drink right now.
How about trying to drink together tomorrow?

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너 그만 마셔, 너 그러다 실수할라!
examples.trans: Stop drinking now—keep going like that and you will slip up!
This expression comes from 'you might make a mistake!'.

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.
It really is strongly, boldly compared to what I thought.
Especially today, it is strongly, boldly and nice.

meanings.note: Combines with 하다 in 말하다 (to speak, to say).

examples.trans: I don't know what you mean.
You speak Korean well.

examples.text: 아무튼 걱정하지 마십시오. 주소 공유 관계는 발설하지 않겠습니다.
examples.trans: Anyway, please do not worry. I will not breathe a word about the address-sharing arrangement.
Forget it, since when have you ever worried about me.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 나는 술이 세단 말이야, 내 걱정하지 말고 너 조절하라고!
examples.trans: I can hold my liquor—stop worrying about me and pace yourself!
This expression comes from 'pace yourself!'.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그 아이 ('that child/kid'); used only for younger people or close peers.

examples.trans: Are you close with her?
He is late every day.

related.gloss: this kid / he or she (near speaker)
that kid / he or she (over there)

meanings.note: reflexive pronoun referring back to the subject

examples.trans: You have to look after your own rice bowl.
Do your own work yourself.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.
I'm on my way home right now.
On weekends I usually rest at home.
I live in Seoul.
Where do you live?

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: ㄹ drops before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 사는데요, 삽니다)
Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 너 나 준모네 집에 산다고 소문냈어, 안 냈어?
examples.trans: Did you spread rumors that I live at Joon-mo's place, or not?
This expression comes from 'did you spread rumors'.

examples.text: 지는 티 안 내려고 무지 애쓰는데 원래 티가 나는 거예요.
examples.trans: He tries hard not to let it show, but feelings like that always show.

examples.text: 티 안 내려고 무지 애는 쓰시는데 저는 조금 알 것 같습니다.
examples.trans: She tries hard not to show it, yet I think I understand that feeling a little.
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: 1st person plural pronoun; also used for 'my' with family, school, or workplace

examples.trans: Our team has a good atmosphere.
Let's eat lunch together tomorrow.

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.trans: Yes, let's each head to our own separate homes, senior!
Here the word for 'each person's own' is key.

meanings.en: first of all, for starters, for the time being
meanings.note: marks an immediate first step before dealing with anything else

examples.trans: Let's sit down and talk first.
Let's wait until today for now.

meanings.note: Contraction of 아이.
Colloquially used to refer to people of the same age or younger.

examples.trans: Kids are running around and playing in the park.
That person has a really good personality.
Did you hear about this as a secret?
I was busy today because of as a secret.

없어지다.gloss: to disappear, vanish; to be cancelled

meanings.note: something ceases to exist or be present
used for shows, programs, or policies being discontinued

examples.trans: The key that was on the desk disappeared.
That program was cancelled last year.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 일단 취하면 애가 비밀이 없어지고 애교가 많아져요.
examples.trans: Once she gets drunk, she has zero secrets left and turns overly cute.
Here the word for 'cutesy charm' is key.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (verb).

examples.text: 일단 취하면 애가 비밀이 없어지고 애교가 많아져요.
examples.trans: Once she gets drunk, she has zero secrets left and turns overly cute.
This expression comes from 'becomes excessive'.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 걔는 어떻게 된 게 중간이 없어, 극단적인 애교!
examples.trans: Somehow she has no middle ground whatsoever—just extreme cuteness!
Here the word for 'middle ground' is key.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 걔는 어떻게 된 게 중간이 없어, 극단적인 애교!
examples.trans: Somehow she has no middle ground whatsoever—just extreme cuteness!
Here the word for 'extreme' is key.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
